name: @txtscape/mcp

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Read a .txt page from project memory. Returns content and a _meta.hash for optimistic concurrency (pass to put_page/str_replace_page/append_page as expected_hash).

path.description: Page path relative to .txtscape/pages/. Must end in .txt. Folder names: lowercase alphanumeric/hyphens/underscores, max 50 chars. Max 10 levels deep. Example: decisions/use-flat-files.txt

tools.name: put_page
tools.description: Create or update a .txt page in project memory. Folders are created automatically. Max 1MB per page. Path must end in .txt. Folder names: lowercase alphanumeric/hyphens/underscores, max 50 chars each, max 10 levels deep. Supports optimistic concurrency: pass expected_hash (from get_page) to prevent stale overwrites.

content.description: Plain text content (markdown formatting supported). Maximum 1MB.

expected_hash.description: Optional. SHA-256 hash from get_page. If provided and doesn't match current file hash, the update is rejected to prevent stale overwrites.

path.description: Page path relative to .txtscape/pages/. Must end in .txt. Folder names: lowercase alphanumeric/hyphens/underscores, max 50 chars. Max 10 levels deep. Example: decisions/use-flat-files.txt

tools.name: append_page
tools.description: Append content to an existing .txt page in project memory. Creates the page if it doesn't exist. Max 1MB total size.

content.description: Text to append to the end of the page.

expected_hash.description: Optional. SHA-256 hash from get_page for optimistic concurrency.

path.description: Page path relative to .txtscape/pages/. Must end in .txt.

tools.name: delete_page
tools.description: Delete a .txt page from project memory.

path.description: Page path relative to .txtscape/pages/. Must end in .txt. Example: decisions/use-flat-files.txt

tools.name: move_page
tools.description: Move/rename a .txt page in project memory. Destination folders are created automatically. Fails if destination already exists.

new_path.description: New page path. Must end in .txt. Folder names: lowercase alphanumeric/hyphens/underscores, max 50 chars. Max 10 levels deep.

path.description: Current page path. Must end in .txt.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: List files and folders in project memory. Returns the first line of each file as a preview. Pass empty path or '/' to list the root. By default, lists all files recursively with full paths. Set recursive=false for a shallow folder-only listing.

path.description: Folder path to list, or empty/'/' for root. Folder names: lowercase alphanumeric/hyphens/underscores, max 50 chars. Example: decisions

recursive.description: If false, list only immediate children (folders with icons, files with previews). Default: true (recursive).

tools.name: search_pages
tools.description: Search across all pages in project memory. Returns matching lines with surrounding context. Returns up to 100 matches, case-insensitive. Supports regex with isRegex=true.

isRegex.description: If true, treat query as a Go regex pattern. Default: false (substring match).

query.description: Text or regex pattern to search for (case-insensitive). Returns up to 100 matches with 1 line of surrounding context each.

tools.name: str_replace_page
tools.description: Replace an exact string in a page with a new string. The old_str must appear exactly once in the page (no ambiguity). Use this for surgical edits without rewriting the whole page.

expected_hash.description: Optional. SHA-256 hash from get_page for optimistic concurrency.

old_str.description: The exact string to find. Must appear exactly once in the page.

path.description: Page path relative to .txtscape/pages/. Must end in .txt.

tools.name: snapshot
tools.description: Read all pages in a subtree and return them concatenated with path headers. Useful for loading all project memory in one call. Pass empty path for the full tree, or a folder path for a subtree. Returns up to 100 pages per call — use offset to paginate.

offset.description: Number of pages to skip (for pagination). Default 0.

path.description: Folder path to snapshot, or empty for root. Example: decisions

tools.name: related_pages
tools.description: Find pages related to a given page. Returns outgoing references (pages mentioned in this page's content) and incoming references (pages that mention this page).

path.description: Page path to find relations for. Must end in .txt.

tools.name: page_history
tools.description: Show the git commit history for a page. Returns commit hashes, dates, and messages. Set include_diff=true to see what changed in each commit. Requires the project to be a git repository.

include_diff.description: If true, include the patch/diff for each commit. Default: false.

limit.description: Maximum number of commits to return. Default: 20.

path.description: Page path to show history for. Must end in .txt.

instructions: journal is this project's local knowledge base, managed by txtscape. Use put_page to store decisions, patterns, and knowledge as .txt files. Use search_pages to find relevant memories. Use list_pages to browse the directory tree with previews. Files are plain text with markdown formatting. All journal pages are stored in .txtscape/pages/ and should be committed to git. When the user says "journal" or "txtscape" or asks you to store or look up project knowledge, they mean this tool. Path rules: files must end in .txt, folder names are lowercase alphanumeric/hyphens/underscores (max 50 chars each), max 10 folder levels deep. File size limit: 1MB per page. Search returns up to 100 matches. Use str_replace_page for surgical edits (old_str must match exactly once). Use snapshot to load all pages in one call. Use related_pages to discover cross-references between pages. Use page_history to see git commit history for a page. get_page returns a hash for optimistic concurrency — pass expected_hash to put_page to prevent stale overwrites.
